precepts.text: None can call on the Lord unless they believe, none believe unless they hear, and none hear without a preacher who is sent to guide and instruct.
precepts.point: No one comes to the truth alone; the Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

precepts.why:
“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

None can call on the Lord unless they believe, none believe unless they hear, and none hear without a preacher who is sent to guide and instruct. That is Jehoash: he “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.”

No one comes to the truth alone. The Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation.

precepts.point: This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned; all things touching the body must be put in writing.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

precepts.why:
“Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.”

That is how the money for the house was handled. Jehoiada set a chest with a hole bored in the lid beside the altar, and when there was much money the king’s scribe and the high priest came up, “and told the money that was found in the house of the Lord”, and gave it into the hands of them that did the work.

This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned. All things touching the body must be put in writing.

points: Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu and reigned forty years in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash ordered that all the dedicated money brought into the house be gathered by the priests to repair the breaches of the house.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: But by the twenty-third year of his reign the priests still had not repaired the breaches, though he had come to power around age seven.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash called Jehoiada and the priests, asked why the house was not repaired, and directed that the money no longer be received by them but delivered directly for the repairs.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in the lid, and set it beside the altar, and the priests put in all the money brought to the house.
This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned; all things touching the body must be put in writing.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: When there was much money, the king's scribe and the high priest counted it and gave it into the hands of the workmen who oversaw the repair.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: The money went to carpenters, builders, masons, and for timber and stone, and none was diverted to make vessels; the workmen dealt faithfully so no reckoning was needed.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Hazael king of Syria took Gath and set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash took the hallowed things dedicated by the former kings, and the gold from the treasures, and sent them to Hazael, who then went away.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: His own servants made a conspiracy and slew Joash in the house of Millo, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
